segmentation.text: about to enter or exit a controlled-access highway
to all vehicles approaching on the highway
whose proximity constitutes an immediate hazard
until the driver may proceed with reasonable safety.

elements.justification: Vehicle aggregate; the driver read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

st.controlled_access 'a highway with access only at designated points, and its entrance and exit lanes'; 'about to' read by the movement it leads to: entry into or exit from the controlled-access region (rel.occupies changing), onto another st.highway region at an exit.

The referent of 'that traffic': vehicles y (aggregate) moving (drv.motion.moving) on the highway being entered (rel.occupies of the controlled-access region at an entry, of the st.highway region x moves onto at an exit).
Continuing to yield is not making the entry or exit (x's overlap with the controlled-access region changing, rel.occupies) while moving (drv.motion.moving) before it may proceed safely.

'That traffic' (DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, 'vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') refers to the vehicles of s4-s5 whose proximity was an immediate hazard; the rule reads them as traffic members of the vehicle aggregate with every qualification s4-s5 state.

operationalizations.standard: whose proximity constitutes an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: Gap acceptance for merging: the body gap (rel.surface_gap) at most the vehicle's speed (kin.speed) times the critical gap.

Traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a predicted closest approach of the two centres under constant velocities within the time-to-collision horizon at a centre distance below the clearance.
Traffic-conflict technique: x may proceed with reasonable safety once no vehicle of that traffic has a predicted closest approach to x within the time-to-collision horizon below the centre clearance.

applicability: x is a vehicle. Judged at each entry of x into a controlled-access region a (x's footprint overlaps a and did not at the observation before) and each exit (it no longer overlaps a and did at the observation before), where there is a vehicle y other than x of that traffic: at some observation of the run of observations immediately before that event during which x stayed on the near side (for an entry, off a; for an exit, on a), y was moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance) on the highway being entered (a at an entry; at an exit, a st.highway region x's footprint overlaps at the exit, not a) with a body gap to x (rel.surface_gap) at most its speed (kin.speed) times p.immediate_hazard_time_gap.
obligation: Where x is moving at the event observation (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance), no vehicle y of that traffic (bound again with its whole selection) has a predicted closest approach to x within p.conflict_time_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
'About to enter or exit' is read by the movement it leads to: the entry into or exit from the controlled-access region.
'Reasonable safety' is read only as the absence of a predicted conflict with that traffic at the moment x proceeds; no other factor is read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x waits on the ramp off a while y on a, 20 m away at 25 m/s, is an immediate hazard; x then enters a while y is still in predicted conflict (1.5 m in 1 s).

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same hazard while x waits; x enters only after y has passed and no conflict with y is predicted.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x enters a with no vehicle on a ever within speed times the critical gap during its approach.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but rel.surface_gap is not observed, so whether y was an immediate hazard is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: x enters a with no other road user in the scene: no hazard arose, so no continued yield is owed.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_time_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a predicted closest approach within this time counts as an imminent conflict.
param_proposals.source: Hayward (1972) time-to-collision; Swedish Traffic Conflict Technique (Hyden 1987)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the predicted closest approach below which two road users' bodies come into conflict: about a passenger car's half-length plus a crossing road user's half-length with a small margin, since the distance is between reference points.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book passenger-car design vehicle dimensions

param_proposals.name: p.immediate_hazard_time_gap
param_proposals.convention: Critical gap of gap acceptance: an approaching vehicle whose time to reach the conflict (its distance over its speed) is at most this gap is an immediate hazard to a turning, crossing or merging manoeuvre.
param_proposals.source: Highway Capacity Manual, base critical headway (4.1 s for a major-street left turn)

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of the acquisition standard (carla_scene_graph kinematics)
